A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EXTAGENTS and the same research problem. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA, survey-generation, ablation, latency and cost results, including additional experiments and qualitative examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, sensitivity experiments, answerability analysis and heterogeneous-model efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The Seeking/Reasoning roles, ranked global synchronization, incremental knowledge accumulation and answerability gate are retained, with matching appendix prompts. v2 clarifies ranking and timing and tests heterogeneous backbones within the existing framework; it introduces no new algorithmic component or training objective.

E1.justification: Both evaluate HotpotQA, English and Chinese ∞Bench+, original ∞Bench and AutoSurvey. The final ∞Bench+ evaluation sets remain 294 English and 184 Chinese samples. Added filtering and component experiments stay within this coverage; newly cited LongBench and RULER are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Chain of Agents, previously only discussed, is evaluated on ∞Bench+ En.QA and Zh.QA with Llama-3.1-8B in v2 Tables 4, 7 and 10. Its reported best F1 scores are 0.168 and 0.246 at 32k input. The other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: Latency evaluation expands from fixed 128k input to 16–1024k inputs with fixed 16k chunks and revised parallelism settings. New protocols include heterogeneous 3B/8B roles at 512k input and 32k chunks, a 371-sample answerability test with four chunks and KAR disabled, and filtering-window and hyperparameter sweeps. These substantially expand the evaluation design while retaining the principal datasets and metrics.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained GKS/KAR ablations and qualitative cases, v2 adds filtering-window sensitivity (Table 3), heterogeneous-role efficiency analysis (Table 6), isolated answerability errors (Table 11), synchronization-limit sensitivity (Table 12) and accumulation-schedule comparisons (Table 13). These examine previously untested design choices and failure modes.

E5.justification: Both report medians of three runs: v1 Section 5.1 and v2 Appendix C.1. Neither adds confidence intervals, seed specifications or significance tests. The new answerability contingency table is an error analysis, while proposed ranking-calibration techniques remain future work.

E6.justification: En.QA curves are numerically revised for EXTAGENTS and LLM×MapReduce with both backbones, including appendix panels. For example, the GPT-4o-mini EXTAGENTS point at 128k input with 8k chunks changes from approximately 0.34 to 0.29 (v1 Figure 5; v2 Figure 10). The PDFs do not explain these revisions. v2 also adds filtering, comparator, answerability, scheduling and heterogeneous-model results and revises latency results. Headline F1 scores remain, but the input accompanying Llama's 0.291 En.QA score changes from 256k to 1024k.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the synchronization recurrence from Top_k(M_t) in v1 Equation 7 to Top_k(M_{t-1}) in Equation 8, aligning it with the previously described previous-round communication. It also specifies intermediate-timestep reasoning messages. The objectives and baseline formalizations remain, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: training-free external-knowledge scaling, the enhanced ∞Bench+ benchmark, overcoming synchronization and reasoning bottlenecks, and improved QA/survey performance with parallel efficiency. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of answerability overconfidence, ranking unreliability, scheduling choices and efficiency tradeoffs, and revises the GKS ablation explanation. The answerability discussion acknowledges 130 incorrect answers judged answerable among 201 incorrect forced answers. The limitations add ranking-calibration concerns but remove v1's specific Broader Tasks transfer caveat. A new linguistic-bias explanation claims better English than Chinese performance, which the cited Table 4 does not establish.

D1.justification: v2 documents two GPUs per model for heterogeneous deployment, supplies explicit input/chunk configurations for additional comparisons, and clarifies distributed per-message scoring. Existing prompts, temperatures, default synchronization settings, baseline implementation descriptions and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds GraphReader, LongBench, RULER, SurveyForge and ranking-calibration literature, with corresponding positioning discussion. It updates model-card coverage and removes the Llama 3 report citation. The retrieval/compression/multi-agent taxonomy remains; publication updates to existing works do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: detailed evaluation settings move to Appendix C.1, limitations and ethics move before the references, and baseline review, qualitative cases and implementation become Appendices A–C. Benchmark, agent-profile and analysis passages are rewritten or condensed, with language and author-header edits throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text and reference layout, replaces Figure 2 with a bottleneck comparison, and redraws Figure 3 to show synchronization ranking explicitly. Existing scaling panels are regrouped across main text and appendices, several tables are added, and the fixed-input latency table is replaced by a scaling plot. These exceed renumbering or numerical updates alone.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful validation of filtering, answerability and accumulation choices, another evaluated baseline, and measured model-role efficiency tradeoffs. Its revised En.QA plots are also more consistent with the headline tables. These improve empirical support and transparency. However, the plot revisions are unexplained, the broader-task transfer caveat is removed, and some new interpretations—including the linguistic-bias claim—remain unsupported, limiting the overall gain.
